How Costco Pays Shareholders

Costco pays a regular quarterly dividend that rose to $1.47 from $1.30, up about 13%. That works out to $5.88 a year. The bigger payouts come irregularly:

$15 per share paid January 12, 2024

The 2024 special by itself came to about 2.6 times the current annual regular payout.

title: What Are Costco Stock Bulls Not Worried About?
detail:
What Are Costco Stock Bulls Not Worried About?
Trefis Team
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 12:51 PM MST 4 min read
COST
^GSPC

TGT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Costco Wholesale (COST) bulls have shown little worry lately: the stock rose 11.3% over the past month while the S&P 500 fell 3.6%. The price appears to assume Costco keeps earning its widest profit margin in years. For that to hold, Costco has to absorb rising costs on oil-related goods and on electronics that use memory chips, and its margin has to stand without help from one-off tariff refunds. So what costs is Costco up against?

Costco Faces Rising Costs That Are Hard To Predict

Costco faces rising costs on goods tied to oil and on the memory inside the electronics it sells. On its September 24, 2026 call, management said it finds it "difficult to predict what's going to happen with inflation." Management pointed to the conflict in the Middle East and to uncertainty over where tariffs land.

These costs already showed up in fiscal Q4 2026. Costco booked a $152 million charge for the higher cost of the goods it holds, compared with $43 million a year earlier. Management said that charge ran well above the quarter's own inflation, because the year-end quarter carries the catch-up for the whole fiscal year. Management also named memory costs in consumer electronics and items such as gas, motor oil and resins as the biggest drivers.

So far, Costco has kept its operating margin: 4.0% in fiscal Q4 2026, against 3.9% in fiscal Q4 2025. Its gross margin on merchandise sales did slip, to 11.02% in fiscal Q4 2026 from 11.13% a year earlier.

How Much Of Costco's Business Do Rising Costs Reach?

The sharpest rises sit in a few corners of Costco, but all $303 billion of its sales over the twelve months to August 2026 run on a single thin margin. Management said non-foods inflation rose in fiscal Q4, mostly from memory costs, gas and petroleum-based items, while food inflation stayed in line with earlier quarters.

Those sales grew 10.1% from a year earlier. Costco kept 3.9% of them as operating profit, compared with 19.0% for the S&P 500. That is Costco's widest twelve-month margin at any quarter end in data going back to fiscal 2017.

That margin is mostly Costco's own. Net of the price cuts Costco funded with them, the tariff refunds added 9 basis points to its fiscal Q4 gross margin, management said. Costco received its initial tariff refunds in that quarter. Without that help, fiscal Q4 net income still rose 12.3% from a year earlier, on management's own measure.

Buyers pay 51.3 times Costco's earnings, compared with 22.3 for the S&P 500. That multiple has ranged from 26.8 to 56.0 at quarter ends since fiscal 2017, so today's sits near the top. The shares also ended November 10 just 2.3% below their highest close of the past year. There is little room in that price for the margin to slip.

Costco's $30 Special Dividend Returns $13.3 Billion. Is It Still a "Good Place to Shelter"? ©@Leung Cho Pan via Canva, @Leung Cho Pan via Canva
Key Takeaways

Costco declared a $30-a-share special dividend worth about $13.3 billion, double its last special in December 2023. It also renewed its $4 billion buyback.

The payout shows Costco makes more cash than it can reinvest: free cash flow was $9.4 billion in fiscal 2026, nearly four times its regular dividends.

Investors pay a premium for that safety: Costco trades at about 47x forward earnings, against a 10-year average of 37x, and Walmart has moved less with the market over five years.

The business still looks like a good place to shelter, but a return to its average multiple would cost the stock about 20%. That makes it a hold for owners and a stock to wait on for new money.

Costco Wholesale (COST:NASDAQ) declared a $30-a-share special dividend after the close on Nov. 10, a payout of about $13.3 billion, and renewed its $4 billion buyback.

Barron's ran the news under the headline "Costco Stock Is a Good Place to Shelter From the AI Chaos." Investors have been doing just that: the stock is up 25% in 2026.

But shelter has gotten pricey. Charlie Bilello set Costco's trailing P/E beside those of Walmart (WMT:NASDAQ) and Nvidia on X last week and asked: "Which one is the bubble?" (Costco's, at about 51x, was the highest of the three.)

Double the last special

The $30 is payable Dec. 4 to shareholders of record on Nov. 24. It's double Costco's last special, $15 a share in December 2023, and about five times its regular dividend of $5.88 a year. The new $4 billion buyback runs to November 2030 and replaces a program under which Costco had bought $3.1 billion of stock. It's small for a company this size: Costco spent $847 million on its own shares in fiscal 2026, less than the $924 million of stock-based compensation it paid.

There are over 100 stocks paying 6%+ annual dividends today.

But after an extensive investment review leveraging TIKR's proprietary data, we now believe only six of them are truly safe for retirees.

They're all yours for free as part of our new investment report, which you can access right here.

The business has earned the label

Costco's business does look built for rough markets. Its U.S. and Canada renewal rate ended fiscal 2026, the year to August, at 92.3%. Comparable sales excluding gas and currency rose between 6.4% and 6.7% in every quarter. Membership fees of $5.9 billion made up half of its $11.7 billion of operating income. title: Costco's $30 Special Dividend Set to Boost Investor Confidence
detail:
Costco's $30 Special Dividend Set to Boost Investor Confidence
Sumit Singh

COST
WMT

Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Costco Wholesale Corporation COST has reinforced its commitment to shareholder returns by announcing a special cash dividend of $30 per share and renewing its stock repurchase authorization. These moves underscore the retailer's financial strength and capital allocation strategy, potentially boosting investor confidence.

Costco declared a special dividend totaling approximately $13.3 billion, payable on Dec. 4 to shareholders of record as of Nov. 24. The substantial distribution highlights the company's ability to return accumulated cash directly to investors, reflecting its strong liquidity position.

Alongside the dividend, Costco's board reauthorized a common-stock repurchase program of up to $4 billion, expiring in November 2030. The authorization replaces the previous $4 billion program, adopted in 2023 and scheduled to expire in January 2027, under which the company had repurchased $3.1 billion in shares.

The timing is particularly notable, given Costco's strengthened balance sheet. At the end of fiscal 2026, cash and cash equivalents stood at $20,207 million, up from $14,161 million in fiscal 2025. Meanwhile, operating cash flow increased to $15,825 million from $13,335 million a year earlier. The improvement demonstrates Costco's ability to generate cash through its operations.

Costco's special dividend offers an immediate shareholder reward, while the renewed buyback authorization provides flexibility for future capital returns. Together, these measures underscore financial discipline and reinforce the retailer's shareholder-friendly approach.

How Are Walmart and Dollar General Rewarding Shareholders?

Walmart Inc. WMT continues to prioritize shareholder returns through dividends and share repurchases. In second-quarter fiscal 2027, Walmart returned approximately $5 billion to shareholders, comprising $2 billion in dividends and $3 billion in share buybacks. The company repurchased 25.7 million shares during the quarter, with $25.1 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization. Walmart's substantial capital returns highlight its strong cash generation and commitment to enhancing shareholder value.

Dollar General Corporation DG is also strengthening shareholder returns through dividends and planned stock repurchases. On its second-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings call, Dollar General declared a quarterly cash dividend of 59 cents per share and announced plans to resume buybacks in the third quarter. The company expects to repurchase up to $700 million in shares during the second half, supported by its improving liquidity position. Dollar General's renewed repurchase activity reinforces its shareholder-friendly capital allocation strategy.

Casey's General Stores (CASY) stock has lost 19.3% in six months, against a 2.2% gain for the S&P 500. Holders appear to be betting that the chain keeps earning more on each gallon of fuel and selling more prepared food as it adds stores. Management will update its full-year guidance with its fiscal second-quarter results, expected on December 7, 2026. Below are the events most likely to move Casey's stock over the next six months.

In its favor

Casey's Profit On Each Gallon Of Fuel

Casey's will show its profit on each gallon of fuel for fiscal Q2 2027 when it reports in December 2026, and in August, the only month management has reported for that quarter, that profit slipped. On its September 9, 2026 call, management said fuel margin was in the low 40s of cents a gallon in August, down from 47.8 cents in the first quarter.

Fuel is a big business for Casey's, bringing in about $448 million of its $1.24 billion in total gross profit last quarter. In fiscal Q1 2027, fuel margin was 6.8 cents a gallon higher than a year earlier, and fuel gross profit rose $73.4 million. So a change of a few cents a gallon matters. Fuel margin per gallon for the whole quarter is the number to watch in the December 2026 report.

The Pace Of New Store Openings

Casey's plans to open at least 120 stores in fiscal 2027, split about evenly between acquisitions and new construction. On its September 9 call, management said the company was on track. New stores matter for what Casey's sells inside them. In the first quarter, prepared food and dispensed beverage earned a 59.3% gross margin, against 35.6% for grocery and general merchandise.

Management guides $800 million of spending on property and equipment for fiscal 2027, which includes remodeling the Cefco stores Casey's took over in the Fikes acquisition. The number of stores opened so far in fiscal 2027 is the figure to watch in the December 2026 and March 2027 reports.

The firm said stronger Walmart U.S. comparable-sales growth, excluding health and wellness, and greater confidence in its marketplace and advertising businesses are needed to support faster EPS growth next year, according to Investing.com.

On Tuesday, Mizuho raised its price target to $135 from $125, maintaining an 'Outperform' rating, and estimates Walmart's global GMV at approximately $765 billion.

Walmart is scheduled to report Q3 results on Nov. 19 before the market opens, with analysts expecting EPS of $0.64 on revenue of approximately $187.22 billion, according to Fiscal.ai estimates.

Walmart (WMT) shares drew investor attention on Wednesday after Bank of America (BofA) raised its price target on the retailer, highlighting its market-share opportunities and growing digital marketplace business.

BofA analyst Christopher Nardone raised the firm's price target on Walmart to $139 from $126 while maintaining a 'Buy' rating, according to The Fly. The revised price target implies approximately 10.7% upside from Walmart's last closing price.

WMT shares traded 1.19% lower in premarket trading at the time of writing.

Thirty-eight of 43 analysts covering the stock rate it 'Buy' or 'Strong Buy', whereas four rate the stock 'Hold' and one rate it 'Sell', according to Koyfin. Their 12-month price targets range from $81 to $ 155, with an average of $128.70.

BofA's Q3 Estimates, FY Guidance And Growth Outlook

BofA expects Walmart to continue gaining market share across grocery and general merchandise, according to The Fly. The firm also expects Walmart to update its full-year sales and earnings-per-share (EPS) guidance toward the upper end of its previous range.

According to a report published by Investing.com, BofA forecasts third-quarter EPS of $0.63 and Walmart U.S. comparable-sales growth, excluding fuel, of 2.8%.

The firm said the market needs to see an acceleration in Walmart U.S. comparable sales, excluding health and wellness, and greater confidence that its marketplace and advertising businesses can help drive faster EPS growth next year, Investing.com reported.

Mizuho Estimates Walmart's Global GMV At $765B

On Tuesday, Mizuho analyst David Bellinger raised the firm's price target on Walmart to $135 from $125 while maintaining an 'Outperform' rating, according to The Fly.

Mizuho estimates Walmart's U.S. third-party marketplace generates $16 billion to $18 billion in annualized GMV, with total U.S. GMV of approximately $500 billion.
